declaration_date.entry: DR Retained Earnings, CR Dividends Payable

date_of_record.when: Date to determine who receives dividend (shareholders on this date get dividend)
date_of_record.note: Stock price usually drops on ex-dividend date (1 business day before record date)

cash_dividends.declaration: DR Retained Earnings, CR Dividends Payable (or Cash Dividend Payable)
cash_dividends.effect_on_equity: Reduces retained earnings and total equity
cash_dividends.example: Declare $1/share cash dividend on 10,000 outstanding shares. Declaration: DR RE $10,000, CR Div Payable $10,000. Payment: DR Div Payable $10,000, CR Cash $10,000.

property_dividends.description: Distribution of non-cash assets (inventory, investments, equipment)
property_dividends.measurement: Record at FAIR VALUE of asset distributed
property_dividends.gain_or_loss: Recognize gain/loss if FV ≠ book value of asset
property_dividends.declaration: DR Retained Earnings (at FV), CR Property Div Payable (at FV), and adjust asset to FV (recognize gain/loss)
property_dividends.payment: DR Property Div Payable, CR Asset
property_dividends.example: Declare dividend of investment (BV $8K, FV $10K). Declaration: DR Investment $2K, CR Gain $2K (adjust to FV), then DR RE $10K, CR Prop Div Pay $10K. Payment: DR Prop Div Pay $10K, CR Investment $10K.

stock_dividends.definition: Distribution of additional shares to existing shareholders (not cash)

small_stock_dividend.measurement: Use FAIR VALUE (market price) per share
small_stock_dividend.entry: DR Retained Earnings (shares × FV), CR Common Stock Dividend Distributable (shares × par), CR APIC (plug)
small_stock_dividend.example: 10% stock dividend. 10,000 shares outstanding, $1 par, market $20. Distribute 1,000 shares. DR RE $20,000 (1,000×$20), CR CS Div Dist $1,000 (1,000×$1), CR APIC $19,000.

large_stock_dividend.measurement: Use PAR VALUE per share (not market value)
large_stock_dividend.entry: DR Retained Earnings (shares × par), CR Common Stock Dividend Distributable (shares × par)
large_stock_dividend.example: 30% stock dividend. 10,000 shares outstanding, $1 par. Distribute 3,000 shares. DR RE $3,000 (3,000×$1), CR CS Div Dist $3,000.

stock_dividends.distribution: When distributed: DR Common Stock Dividend Distributable, CR Common Stock
stock_dividends.effect_on_equity: Reclassifies within equity (RE to Common Stock and APIC). Total equity UNCHANGED.
stock_dividends.no_cash_effect: Stock dividends do NOT reduce assets or total equity

stock_splits.definition: Increase in number of shares outstanding with proportional decrease in par value per share
stock_splits.effect: Proportionally increases shares and decreases par value per share. Total par value of common stock UNCHANGED.
stock_splits.example_2_for_1: 10,000 shares, $10 par → After split: 20,000 shares, $5 par. Common Stock account remains $100,000. NO entry.
stock_splits.comparison_to_stock_dividend: Stock splits: No entry, change par. Stock dividends: Entry to reclassify RE, par unchanged per share.

reverse_stock_split.definition: Decrease shares, increase par value proportionally
reverse_stock_split.example: 1-for-2 reverse split: 10,000 shares $1 par → 5,000 shares $2 par
reverse_stock_split.purpose: Often used to increase stock price (when trading below $1, at risk of delisting)

small_stock_div.entry: Yes (DR RE at FV, CR CS Div Dist, CR APIC)

large_stock_div.entry: Yes (DR RE at par, CR CS Div Dist)

liquidating_dividend.definition: Dividend that exceeds retained earnings (returns capital to shareholders)
liquidating_dividend.entry: DR Retained Earnings (up to available balance), DR Additional Paid-In Capital (remainder), CR Dividends Payable
liquidating_dividend.disclosure: Must disclose to shareholders that dividend is liquidating (returning capital)

scrip_dividend.definition: Promissory note (IOU) to pay dividend in future
scrip_dividend.entry: DR Retained Earnings, CR Notes Payable (or Scrip Dividend Payable)

calculation_example_complex.facts: 100,000 shares outstanding, $2 par, market $30. Board declares: (1) 5% stock dividend, (2) $0.50/share cash dividend after stock dividend.
calculation_example_complex.step_2_distribution: DR CS Div Dist $10,000, CR Common Stock $10,000. Now 105,000 shares outstanding.

cpa_exam_tips: Declaration date creates liability (record entry). Record date = no entry. Payment date = pay liability.
Small stock dividend (<20-25%): Use FAIR VALUE. Large (≥20-25%): Use PAR VALUE.
Stock split: NO entry (memo only), par value changes
Stock dividend: Entry required (DR RE, CR CS Div Dist), par stays same per share
Property dividend: Record at FV, recognize gain/loss on asset
Treasury stock doesn't receive dividends (only outstanding shares)

identification_framework.cash_dividend: Cash distributed → DR RE, CR Div Payable → Equity decreases
identification_framework.small_stock_div: <20-25% → Use FV → DR RE (shares×FV), CR CS Div Dist (shares×par), CR APIC
identification_framework.large_stock_div: ≥20-25% → Use par → DR RE (shares×par), CR CS Div Dist (shares×par)

calculation_steps: 3. Determine measurement (FV for small stock div, par for large stock div)
4. Record entries at appropriate dates (declaration, distribution/payment)
5. Calculate new shares outstanding after stock div/split
common_mistakes: Using FV for large stock dividend (should be par)
Recording entry for stock split (no entry required)
Forgetting to multiply cash dividend by new shares outstanding if stock dividend occurred first
Including treasury shares in dividend calculations (only outstanding shares)

key_points: Declaration date: Record liability. Record date: No entry. Payment date: Pay liability.
Cash dividend: Reduces RE and total equity
Small stock dividend (<20-25%): DR RE at fair value
Large stock dividend (≥20-25%): DR RE at par value
Stock split: No entry, par value changes proportionally
Property dividend: Use FV, recognize gain/loss
Stock dividends and splits don't reduce total equity (only reclassify)
